outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms continuation of use: obtain an EIN, form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State, register for a seller's permit with CDTFA, and register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: File Form SS-4 online with the IRS for an EIN (same day, free). File LLC-1 or Articles of Incorporation with the California Secretary of State via bizfile Online ($70–$150, 1–10 days). Register for a California Seller's Permit online with CDTFA (free, often same day). Register the business with SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector online to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN); the fee is tiered by gross receipts, starting at $55 for revenues under $100k plus a $4 state fee (1–5 days). File a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk if the DBA differs from the legal name, then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof within 45 days ($60–$120 filing fee).

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms continuation of use: submit DPH plan check application online for the kitchen remodel with the BAN, federal tax ID, scaled drawings, equipment list, menu and finishes schedule. What to say: Apply through the DPH Environmental Health portal at least 60 days before the target opening. State that this is a continuation of an existing limited-restaurant use with tenant improvements, citing the 2014 Planning approval (MB1400941). The flat fee for a small remodel (limited cooking, under 2,000 sq ft) is about $828 (3 hours review time), with extra review billed at $276/hour if the plans are incomplete. Include two sets of scaled drawings showing equipment layout, three-compartment sinks, hand sinks within 15 feet of food prep, hot and cold water, sealed surfaces and ventilation. Request a pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and schedule the final inspection two weeks in advance. Name your plan reviewer and keep their contact information.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms continuation of use: one owner or employee must pass an accredited food-safety certification exam within 60 days of opening, and all food-handling employees must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire. What to say: Register the certified food protection manager for a ServSafe, Prometric or other ANSI-accredited exam ($100–$250, results in 1–14 days). The certificate is valid for five years and must be on site for DPH inspections. Every employee who handles food must complete an ANSI-accredited online Food Handler course ($7–$15, about two hours, valid three years). Keep the roster on site. Do this before the DPH pre-opening inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If Planning confirms continuation of use: apply for the Health Permit to Operate online at least 30 days before opening, after DPH approves the plans and the building permit is issued. What to say: Submit the application through the DPH Environmental Health portal with the BAN, Location ID (LIN), federal tax ID, and proof that a certified food manager is on staff. The FY2026–27 fee is $470 for the Permit to Operate application (includes the initial inspection); the annual license fee for restaurants and bars was $0 for 2026–28. Schedule the pre-opening inspection after construction is at least 90% complete and all equipment is installed and operational. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection: verify hand sinks, sealed surfaces, hot water, thermometers, test strips and posted handwashing signs. A failed inspection pushes opening by 2–3 weeks. The permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans. You cannot serve the public before the permit is issued.
outcomes.note: Record doesn't state the timing requirement about DPH plan approval and building permit, portal name, when to schedule inspection or 90% threshold, or several specific checklist items.

What to say: Every person serving or managing alcohol must complete AB 1221 Responsible Beverage Service training within 60 days of hire: register on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), take an approved course ($10–$25), pass the exam (1–7 days total). Workers' compensation insurance is mandatory from the first employee (quote through a broker or State Fund; premiums are a percentage of payroll, typically 2–6% for restaurant class codes). If you install new exterior signage, file a sign permit…

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,600 to $21,500. Notes: This is the time and government cost to obtain Conditional Use Authorization, Health Permit to Operate, Building Permit with change of use, and ABC Type 41 licence when those approvals are granted. The ranges assume the concept requires a CUA hearing (120–300 days for the CUA alone per comparable case 2021-008505CUA, which took 183 days from filing to approval) plus concurrent health plan check (21–60 days), building permit with TI (14–120 days), and ABC Type 41 as a new application in an over-concentrated tract requiring PCN review (60–150 days total per the catalog, longer end if protested). Cost includes CUA application fee of approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted from the 2023–24 no-construction rate of $2,747), DPH plan check $828–$2,500, Health Permit to Operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (percentage of construction valuation), ABC Type 41 $1,000–$1,600, and SF Business Registration $55–$700, totaling roughly $6,300–$23,400 in government fees; the lower bound shown excludes optional items like sign permits and uses minimum building-permit fees. IF PLANNING CONFIRMS CONTINUATION OF USE at Step 1, the pathway collapses to agency referrals with no CUA hearing: health plan check and permit (21–60 + 14–45 days, $828–$2,500 + $470), building permit routed to Planning for zoning sign-off (14–120 days, $800–$15,000), and ABC referral (5–28 days for Planning's part per the comparables, then 60–120 days total for ABC if a new licence, or faster if a transfer), cutting the timeline to roughly 60–180 days and cost to $2,100–$18,600. The cost ranges exclude construction, architect and contractor fees, workers' comp premiums, music-licence subscriptions, and the price of a transferred ABC licence (if that path is chosen). No time or cost is given if Planning determines at Step 1 that the use is not a legal continuation and a new conditional use is not permitted for a restaurant at this address or that formula retail prohibits the concept.
